rv.q: That we come to care at all about these brutes is proof of how well Berger and his actors have risen to the challenge of Titus.
In the end, this is about as effective a take on “Titus Andronicus” as you’re likely to see.
I suspect many theatergoers will purchase tickets just to hear Shakespeare’s words incanted in Page’s gorgeously resonant voice, which rivals that of Vincent Price in its sinister singularity.

What’s more, the spirited Theater revival that opened on Sunday at the Pershing Square Signature Center stars a forceful Patrick Page, whose wily acting, growling baritone vocals and formidable presence lend grandeur and menace to the title character.
And this production pulls it off perfectly.
Instead, we’re left with a flawed revival of an unmistakably flawed play, pushing the envelope in all the wrong places.

cn.t: Red Bull Theater tackles Shakespeare's notoriously bloody early tragedy with spirited boldness, earning mostly positive reviews. Critics praise the production's artistic prowess while noting the play itself remains more fascinating than satisfying.

vr.q: When a company like Red Bull does it with a cast that's this good in a space this intimate, you got to go. You don't wait. You go see it.
if you have the opportunity and if you think you can handle the blood and gore I would recommend it
